result: The authors identified compound heterozygous deleterious variants in ACK1 (K161Q and A156T) in Family 1 and in BRK (G257A and G321R) in Family 2 through whole exome sequencing. These variants segregate with disease in an autosomal recessive pattern and are rare or private to the families.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm the identification of compound heterozygous variants in ACK1 and BRK in familial SLE. The editor states the authors 'found...compound heterozygous rare deletion variants affecting the kinase-domain of non-receptor tyrosine kinase TNK2/ACK1 and PTK6/BRK are associated with human systemic lupus erythematosus.' Reviewers 2 and 3 similarly confirm these findings without raising concerns about the genetic data.

result: The ACK1 and BRK variants strongly decrease kinase activity. In vitro kinase assays showed ACK1 A156T and BRK G321R are kinase-dead mutants, while ACK1 K161Q and BRK G257A are severe hypomorphs with ~20% residual activity. These variants also lack auto-phosphorylation activity and phenocopy specific kinase inhibitors.
evaluation: The reviewers do not question the biochemical characterization of the variants. The editor notes the authors use 'convincing...experimental model' and all reviewers accept that the variants are deleterious and affect kinase activity. No concerns are raised about the in vitro kinase assays or auto-phosphorylation data.

result: ACK1 or BRK inhibitors induce autoantibodies in mice without pristane, and aggravate glomerular IgG deposition and increase autoantibody levels in pristane-treated BALB/cByJ mice. This supports that ACK1/BRK inhibition promotes autoimmunity and may contribute to SLE development.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The experiments in this revision showing that a weekly injection of ACK1 or BRK inhibitors induced various kinds of lupus-related autoantibodies in BALB/c supported the pivotal role of ACK1/BRK in systemic autoimmunity.' However, the reviewer notes 'treated mice failed to demonstrate the full picture of lupus,' indicating the model has limitations but the core finding is accepted.

result: The patients' ACK1 and BRK variants are kinase dead in response to MERTK activation and fail to phosphorylate AKT and STAT3 or activate RAC1. MERTK activated wild-type ACK1 and BRK but not the patient variants.
evaluation: The reviewers do not challenge these biochemical findings. The editor describes the work as using 'convincing...experimental model' and Reviewer 3 states the authors 'reported that ACK and BRK variants from the SLE patients impaired the MERTK-mediated anti-inflammatory response,' implicitly accepting the signaling defects.

result: Human iPSC-derived macrophages from patients showed defective AKT/STAT3-driven anti-inflammatory response to apoptotic cells, failed to upregulate anti-inflammatory gene sets, and did not suppress TNF and IL1β production in response to apoptotic cells. ACK1 and BRK kinase activities are required for the anti-inflammatory response during efferocytosis.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly states the authors 'reported that ACK and BRK variants from the SLE patients impaired the MERTK-mediated anti-inflammatory response to apoptotic cells in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC)-derived macrophages.' The editor notes the use of 'convincing...hiPSC-derived macrophages to clarify cause-effect relationships.' No concerns are raised about these functional studies.

result: Patient macrophages showed altered actin-ring formation and reduced actin clearance factor in frustrated engulfment assays, and had a modest 10-20% reduction in engulfment of apoptotic cells. ACK1 and BRK kinase activity contribute to phagocytic synapse formation but are largely dispensable for engulfment.
evaluation: The reviewers do not question these findings about the modest engulfment defect. The data showing ACK1/BRK are more important for anti-inflammatory response than engulfment itself is accepted without challenge. The distinction between these two aspects of efferocytosis is implicitly supported by the reviewers' acceptance of the overall conclusions.

result: ACK1 and BRK kinase activity are dispensable for phagocytosis of polystyrene beads, opsonized cells, and microbes (bacteria and fungi). The kinase deficiency does not cause a global engulfment defect.
evaluation: The reviewers do not challenge these specificity controls. The data showing selective effects on apoptotic cell uptake versus other phagocytic cargos support the mechanistic interpretation and are accepted without comment.

result: iPSCs were generated from patients and controls, and hiPSC-derived macrophages showed normal morphology, survival, phenotype, and comparable expression of ACK1 and BRK at transcript and protein levels.
evaluation: The reviewers do not raise concerns about the iPSC generation or characterization. The editor notes the use of 'convincing...hiPSC-derived macrophages' and all reviewers accept the cellular model system.

result: Analysis of 27 GWAS studies found no common variants near ACK1 or BRK genes with genome-wide significance. ACK1 and BRK deficiency likely account for SLE in only a minority of patients and probably underlie development in a small proportion of children and young adults.
evaluation: The reviewers accept this interpretation about the rarity of these genetic causes. The editor describes this as identifying 'a rare Mendelian cause of severe SLE' and Reviewer 3 states the work 'identified new SLE-associated ACK and BRK variants,' implicitly accepting they are rare causes.

result: The study identifies a rare Mendelian cause of severe SLE and establishes a role for TNK2/ACK1 and PTK6/BRK in efferocytosis. These kinase deficiencies impair the MERTK-dependent anti-inflammatory response more than engulfment itself, contributing to the autoimmune phenotype.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly support these main conclusions. The editor calls this 'an important study' that 'improves our understanding of human SLE pathogenesis.' Reviewer 3 states 'This work identified new SLE-associated ACK and BRK variants and a role for the NRTK TNK2/ACK1 and PTK6/BRK in efferocytosis, providing a new molecular and cellular mechanism of SLE pathogenesis.'
